evidence: createApp registers Express routes and passes every operation to service.* methods (placeOrder, advance, cancel, addProduct, stockLevels, listOrders, getOrder).
The STATUS constant and the error middleware turn DomainError codes into HTTP status codes, which is transport concern.
view(o: Order) turns the domain object into a JSON response DTO (placedAt.toISOString()), which is presentation/transport serialization.
The ACTIONS table maps URL action segments (pay/pack/ship/deliver) to target OrderState. Transition validity is enforced by service.advance, not here.
`if (!Array.isArray(body.items)) throw new DomainError("invalid", ...)` checks the request's shape at the boundary. It is not a business rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http-app.ts is an Express HTTP adapter. Everything it does is transport work, which belongs in the infrastructure layer: it sets up routes, parses request params, query strings and bodies, shapes response views, and maps DomainError codes to HTTP status codes in an error middleware. Business operations such as placing orders, advancing state, cancelling, adding products and checking stock levels are all handed to OrderService in the application layer. The ACTIONS table only maps URL path segments to target states. Which state transitions are allowed is still decided by the service and domain, as the separate invalid_transition error code shows. The Array.isArray check on items only checks the shape of the request at the transport boundary. It is not a business rule. No persistence or domain invariants are implemented here.
